subject.title: fix(infra): lack of transactional safety during doctor fix migrations

question: Should plugin doctor migrations gain a supported synchronous atomic-batch transaction seam, or should each plugin remain responsible for idempotent checkpointed writes and complete-target verification?
rationale: The existing plugin contract is asynchronous and exposes independently transactional keyed stores; safely fixing the class requires choosing the permanent plugin/core ownership boundary rather than wrapping the whole doctor flow in a transaction.

options.title: Add atomic batch seam
options.body: Expose a narrow synchronous plugin-state migration transaction API and migrate multi-namespace imports to prepare asynchronously and commit related rows together.

options.title: Require resumable checkpoints
options.body: Keep the existing store API but require every migration to checkpoint per item and verify all expected namespaces or keys before treating the source as complete.

options.title: Patch known migration only
options.body: Repair the demonstrated Memory Core path now and track a separate audit of sibling plugin migrations, accepting that equivalent gaps may remain temporarily.

recommendation.title: Add atomic batch seam
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow synchronous plugin-state migration transaction API and migrate multi-namespace imports to prepare asynchronously and commit related rows together.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared SQLite database and plugin doctor SDK ownership boundaries trace most strongly to this history, making this the best available routing candidate for the contract decision.
